title: Adaptive cohort-driven A/B orchestrator with drift-aware early-stop and shadow replay
creator: Natalie Chen
description:
Goal: Ship an A/B experiment orchestration layer that enables safe, low-friction model variant rollouts by combining cohort stratification, drift-aware sequential checks, shadow traffic replay, and automated rollback policies. This work is focused on the product-facing experiment setup UX, a policy engine for exposure control, and the statistical guardrails that enable early-stop decisions without sacrificing statistical rigor.

Problem statement: Teams frequently need to compare model variants in production while minimizing user exposure and limiting noise from distribution shifts. Current rollouts either rely on static canaries or ad-hoc metrics, which creates longer rollouts and manual rollbacks. We need a standardized framework that: 1) targets cohorts deterministically, 2) detects input/output drift early, 3) performs sequential statistical checks tuned for LLM outputs, and 4) offers safe automated rollback and shadow replay for diagnostic runs.

Key features and scope: 
- Experiment creation: templated setup for A/B and canary experiments (variant definitions, sampling rules, cohort stratifiers: geography, platform, user-tier, request latency buckets).
- Exposure controller: programmable ramp policies (linear, power curve, adaptive) with min/max exposure, cool-down windows, and manual override.
- Drift detector: streaming input and output distribution monitoring (token length, embedding drift via cosine/KS proxy, top-k rerank changes) with thresholds that trigger additional checks.
- Sequential analysis: Bayesian sequential probability ratio testing and nonparametric sign tests for utility metrics (CTR, task completion, hallucination rate). Supports conservative stopping boundaries and false-discovery-rate adjustments when running multiple metrics.
- Shadow replay mode: ability to mirror traffic to a candidate variant (no user exposure) with side-by-side comparison in dashboards; captures both deterministic and sampling-based modes.
- Auto-rollback: configurable rollback rules tied to metric breaches (absolute or relative), with cooldown and ramp-down policies and an audit trail for each automated action.
- Observability & alerts: per-experiment dashboards, signal decomposition (which cohorts failing), integrated alerts to Slack and PagerDuty with suggested remediation steps.
- Console & API integration: Surfaces experiment controls in Redwood Console; full API/SDK endpoints for programmatic orchestration and CI-driven experiments.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Product UX: Create an experiment in Console that specifies variants, cohort stratifiers, and a ramp policy.
2) Runtime: Exposure controller enforces routing to variants per policy with <100ms routing decision overhead in hosted mode.
3) Metrics: System computes sequential tests and reports stop/continue decisions within the configured cooldown window.
4) Shadow: Shadow replay can be enabled per-route; captured outputs are visible in a comparison view and linked to request IDs.
5) Auto-rollback: When metric breach rules are hit in two consecutive windows, the platform performs an automated rollback and records a signed audit event.
6) Integrations: Dashboard, alerting, and an example GitHub actions workflow to gate PRs on experiment success.

Out of scope: Full-blown population-level causal inference, offline meta-analysis toolkit, or custom ML model training pipelines. This is an orchestration and safety/observability layer for production inference variants.
